Export a fitted model to Mplus

to_mplus.Rd

Writes the analysed data and an Mplus input file that specifies the same model, so that the fit can be reproduced or audited in Mplus.

Usage

to_mplus(
  model,
  file,
  datafile = NULL,
  svalues = TRUE,
  categorical = "ordinal",
  tight = TRUE,
  run = FALSE,
  mplus = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  analysis = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A fitted latentmix model.

file

Path of the Mplus input (.inp) file to write.

datafile

Path of the data file; default: file with extension .dat. Keep it in the folder of file (Mplus reads it by its relative path).

svalues

Logical; use the estimates as starting values with STARTS = 0 (TRUE) or random starts as in the fit (FALSE).

categorical

"ordinal" (CATEGORICAL, thresholds) or "nominal" (NOMINAL, multinomial intercepts); both specify the same unrestricted latent class model.

tight

Logical; tighter EM convergence criteria than the Mplus defaults, close to the criterion of the R fit.

run

Logical; run Mplus on the input (needs Mplus, see mplus).

mplus

Path of the Mplus executable; default: the MPLUS environment variable, mplus on the PATH, or /Applications/Mplus/mplus.

title, analysis

Optional TITLE and extra ANALYSIS options (e.g. "PROCESSORS = 4;").

Value

Invisibly, a list with inp, dat and out (the paths written; out is NULL unless run = TRUE) and names, a data frame of the original and the Mplus variable names.

Details

Every model type of the package is supported: LCA (indicators CATEGORICAL or NOMINAL), LPA (all variance/covariance structures), one-step covariates (c ON x), sampling weights (WEIGHT), multigroup models (KNOWNCLASS; invariance through equality labels), LTA (any invariance, time-specific or stationary transitions), LCGA, GMM and parallel-process growth models.

With svalues = TRUE (default) every free parameter gets the estimate of model as its starting value (as Mplus OUTPUT: SVALUES prints them) and STARTS = 0, so Mplus converges to the same solution with the classes in the same order. Variable names are shortened to the Mplus limit of 8 characters if needed (y1, y2, ...; the mapping is returned and written as comments in the input); categorical indicators are coded 0, ..., C - 1 in the data file.

See also

compare_mplus() to compare the Mplus output with the R fit.

Examples

# \donttest{
m <- lca(read.table(system.file("extdata", "lca_bin.dat", package = "latentmixtures"),
                    na.strings = "-999"), K = 3, starts = c(50, 10))
#> Starting Julia ...
f <- file.path(tempdir(), "lca3.inp")
r <- to_mplus(m, f)
readLines(r$inp, n = 12)
#>  [1] "TITLE: LatentMixtures.jl LCA model, K = 3;"                                           
#>  [2] "  ! written by LatentMixtures.jl to_mplus; Julia log-likelihood -6562.223295, npar 26"
#>  [3] "DATA: FILE = \"lca3.dat\";"                                                           
#>  [4] "VARIABLE:"                                                                            
#>  [5] "  NAMES = v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v8;"                                                   
#>  [6] "  USEVARIABLES = v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v8;"                                            
#>  [7] "  MISSING = ALL(-999);"                                                               
#>  [8] "  CATEGORICAL = v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 v7 v8;"                                             
#>  [9] "  CLASSES = c(3);"                                                                    
#> [10] "ANALYSIS: TYPE = MIXTURE; ESTIMATOR = MLR;"                                           
#> [11] "  STARTS = 0;"                                                                        
#> [12] "  MCONVERGENCE = 1E-8; LOGCRITERION = 1E-9; RLOGCRITERION = 1E-12;"                   
if (nzchar(Sys.which("mplus"))) compare_mplus(m, to_mplus(m, f, run = TRUE)$out)
# }
